title: Dirichlet L-functions and primes in progressions
summary: $L(s,\chi) = \sum \chi(n) n^{-s} = \prod_p (1-\chi(p)p^{-s})^{-1}$. Dirichlet (1837) proved $L(1,\chi) \ne 0$ for $\chi \ne \chi_0$, so every progression $a \bmod q$ with $\gcd(a,q)=1$ has infinitely many primes.
references: Apostol, Introduction to Analytic Number Theory

leads_to.title: Siegel zeros and the Landau–Siegel problem

title: Dirichlet's class number formula
summary: Dirichlet (1839) expressed $L(1,\chi_D)$ through the class number of forms of discriminant $D$. For $D < -4$, $L(1,\chi_D) = \pi h(D)/\sqrt{|D|}$.
why: It turns the non-vanishing of $L(1,\chi)$ into the positivity of a class number, and links Siegel zeros to small class numbers.
references: Cox, Primes of the Form x² + ny²

title: Siegel zeros and the Landau–Siegel problem
summary: A real character $\chi$ might have $L(\beta,\chi) = 0$ with $\beta$ extremely close to $1$. Siegel (1935) proved $1 - \beta \gg_\varepsilon q^{-\varepsilon}$, but the constant cannot be computed. Excluding such zeros was a central open problem.
why: A Siegel zero would make primes unevenly spread among residue classes and class numbers unexpectedly small.

timeline.title: Siegel's theorem

title: The Siegel–Walfisz theorem
summary: For any fixed $A$, primes up to $x$ split evenly among residue classes modulo $q \le (\log x)^A$, with error $O(x e^{-c\sqrt{\log x}})$. The constant is ineffective because it relies on Siegel's theorem.
key_statements: \psi(x; q, a) = \frac{x}{\varphi(q)} + O_A\!\bigl(x\, e^{-c\sqrt{\log x}}\bigr), \quad q \le (\log x)^A
why: It is the input for Vinogradov's three-primes theorem and for Bombieri–Vinogradov.

title: Sieves from Eratosthenes to Brun
summary: The sieve of Eratosthenes, written with inclusion–exclusion, is the Legendre identity. Brun (1919) truncated it and proved $\sum 1/p$ over twin primes converges, the first result on twin primes.
why: Sieves estimate how many integers survive after removing residue classes, which is the right question for twin primes and Goldbach.
references: Montgomery & Vaughan, Multiplicative Number Theory I

timeline.title: Brun's theorem
timeline.text: The sum of reciprocals of twin primes converges.

title: The Selberg sieve
summary: Selberg (1947) replaced $\mu(d)$ by weights $\lambda_d$ chosen to minimise a quadratic form, giving sharp upper bounds such as $\pi(x+y) - \pi(x) \le (2+o(1))\,y/\log y$.
why: The same idea, applied with many linear forms at once, is the engine of Maynard's 2013 proof of bounded gaps.

timeline.title: The Selberg sieve

timeline.title: Multidimensional sieve and Polymath8
timeline.text: A new sieve for bounded gaps; the collaborative project lowered the bound to $246$.

title: The large sieve
summary: An inequality bounding a trigonometric polynomial at well-spaced points (Linnik, 1941). With characters it says no sequence can be badly distributed in many residue classes at once.
key_statements: \sum_{q \le Q}\ \sum_{\substack{a \bmod q \\ (a,q)=1}} \Bigl|\sum_{n \le N} a_n e\!\left(\tfrac{an}{q}\right)\Bigr|^2 \le (N + Q^2)\sum_n |a_n|^2
references: Montgomery & Vaughan, Multiplicative Number Theory I
